es: Comparar predicciones con otra persona: dar tu opinión, dudar con cortesía y acordar cuáles son más probables.

teaching.en: Which idea is the most likely to change our lives by 2035?
teaching.es: ¿Qué idea es la más probable que cambie nuestras vidas para 2035?
segments: Which idea is the most likely
teaching.audioText: Which idea is the most likely to change our lives by 2035?

teaching.en: In my opinion, robot taxis will be working in our city by 2040.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, los taxis robot estarán funcionando en nuestra ciudad para 2040.
teaching.explanationEs: In my opinion introduce tu punto de vista; después, will be + gerundio.
segments: In my opinion, robot taxis will be
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, robot taxis will be working in our city by 2040.

teaching.en: I see your point, but I think it is unlikely.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu punto, pero creo que es poco probable.
teaching.explanationEs: I see your point reconoce la idea del otro antes de dudar con cortesía.
teaching.audioText: I see your point, but I think it is unlikely.

teaching.en: I disagree a little, because there is a good chance that cars will have become electric by then.
teaching.es: No estoy del todo de acuerdo, porque hay una buena posibilidad de que para entonces los coches ya se hayan vuelto eléctricos.
teaching.explanationEs: Disagree + because da la razón; chance = posibilidad.
segments: I disagree a little, because there is a good
chance that cars will have become electric by then.
teaching.audioText: I disagree a little, because there is a good chance that cars will have become electric by then.

teaching.en: Let us make a list: which three ideas are the most likely?
teaching.es: Hagamos una lista: ¿cuáles son las tres ideas más probables?
teaching.explanationEs: Let us + verbo base propone hacer algo juntos.
segments: Let us make a list: which
three ideas are the most likely?
teaching.audioText: Let us make a list: which three ideas are the most likely?

teaching.en: Our final list: apps will have replaced keys by 2035, and robots will be helping at home.
teaching.es: Nuestra lista final: para 2035 las aplicaciones habrán sustituido a las llaves y los robots estarán ayudando en casa.
teaching.explanationEs: La lista final reúne predicciones con will have y will be.
segments: Our final list: apps will have replaced keys by
2035, and robots will be helping at home.
teaching.audioText: Our final list: apps will have replaced keys by 2035, and robots will be helping at home.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase duda con cortesía de la idea de tu amigo?

choices.text: No, that is wrong and it is unlikely.
I see your point, but I think it is unlikely.
I see your point, but it will unlikely.

feedback.es: Primero se reconoce la idea (I see your point) y luego se duda con but I think it is unlikely.

hint.es: Reconoce la idea del otro antes de dudar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es probable que los robots estén ayudando en casa.»

feedback.es: Likely se construye con to + verbo base: are likely to be helping.

hint.es: Tras likely va una palabra corta antes del verbo.

origin.text: Robots are likely ___ be helping at home.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase propone añadir una idea a la lista del grupo?

choices.text: Let us to put robot doctors in our list.
Let us putting robot doctors on our list.
Let us put robot doctors on our list.

feedback.es: Let us + verbo base propone hacer algo juntos: Let us put...

hint.es: Tras let us va el verbo base, sin to ni -ing.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En mi opinión, los robots estarán ayudando en los hospitales.»

answer.text: In my opinion robots will be helping in hospitals

feedback.es: In my opinion presenta tu punto de vista; will be helping muestra la acción en curso.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina Leo sobre los profesores robot.

choices.text: He does not think teachers will be replaced.
He thinks robots will replace every teacher.
He agrees with Mia.

feedback.es: Leo reconoce la idea pero dice I disagree y will not have replaced: para 2035 no los habrán sustituido.

origin.audio: Leo says: I see your point, but I disagree. Robot teachers will not have replaced real teachers by 2035.

prompt.es: Lee el debate. ¿Por qué duda Leo de los taxis voladores?

choices.text: Taxis will be too cheap.
The battery will not be ready.
Nobody will want to fly.

feedback.es: Leo duda porque los ingenieros no habrán terminado la batería.

origin.text: Mia: Flying taxis will be working by 2030. Leo: I disagree. The chance is small because engineers will not have finished the battery.

prompt.es: Escribe tu parte del debate: opinión, duda cortés y acuerdo final.

answer.text: In my opinion, robot taxis are unlikely by 2035. I see your point, but the batteries will not have improved enough by then, so the chance is small. However, electric cars will probably be working in every city. Let us put electric cars on our list, and we can talk about robot taxis again in 2040. I think we agree on that.
accepted: In my opinion, robot taxis are unlikely by 2035. I see your point, but the batteries will not have improved enough by then, so the chance is small. However, electric cars will probably be working in every city. Let us put electric cars on our list, and we can talk about robot taxis again in 2040. I think we agree on that.

I think robot taxis are unlikely in 2035. I see your point, but the engineers will not have finished the batteries by then. The chance is small. Electric cars will probably be working in our city, so let us put them on our list. We agree on that, and we can talk about taxis later.

feedback.es: Un buen turno de debate da una opinión, reconoce la idea del otro, explica la duda con will not have y propone el acuerdo con Let us.

origin.text: Tu amigo dice que los taxis robot estarán funcionando en tu ciudad en 2035. Tú crees que es poco probable porque las baterías no estarán listas. Da tu opinión, reconoce su idea, explica tu duda y acuerda poner los coches eléctricos en la lista.

prompt.es: Escucha el debate y elige qué opina Tom.

choices.text: He is sure phones will disappear.
He will buy glasses in 2035.
He is not sure that phones will disappear.

feedback.es: Tom dice I am not sure y unlikely: duda de que los móviles vayan a desaparecer.

origin.audio: Mia: By 2035, most of us will be using glasses instead of phones. Tom: I am not sure. I think it is unlikely, because people like their phones.

prompt.es: Elige la frase con la forma correcta tras «by the time».

choices.text: By the time we finish the list, the lab will have closed.
By the time we will finish the list, the lab will have closed.
By the time we finish the list, the lab will close.

feedback.es: By the time va con presente simple (finish) y la otra parte, con will have + participio.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para 2040, las baterías habrán mejorado mucho.»

feedback.es: By 2040 pide future perfect: will have + participio (improved).

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cierra un debate con un acuerdo?

choices.text: OK, we disagree. Our list has three ideas.
OK, we agree. Our list has three ideas.
OK, we agree. Our list have three ideas.

feedback.es: We agree cierra el acuerdo y list va con has (singular). We disagree contradice el cierre.

prompt.es: Da tu opinión sobre si los robots estarán en las casas en 2040.

answer.text: In my opinion, robots are likely to be in our homes.
accepted: In my opinion, robots are likely to be in our homes.
I think robots are likely to be in our homes.
In my opinion, robots will probably be in our homes.

feedback.es: La opinión se abre con in my opinion o I think, y la probabilidad se dice con likely to o will probably.

origin.text: Opinión: es probable. Usa in my opinion o I think y la idea de que es probable.

prompt.es: Escucha a Sara y elige qué piensa de la idea de Carlos.

choices.text: She thinks it is certain.
She thinks it has already happened.
She thinks it is unlikely.

feedback.es: Sara dice I disagree y only a small chance: para ella es poco probable.

origin.audio: I disagree, Carlos. There is only a small chance that robots will have replaced all the doctors by 2040.
